Adding a digital version of a driver's license to iPhone looks set to launch in a 15th US state soon.

Apple currently lists 14 states plus Puerto Rico that support the feature, and backend assets indicate another is on the way...

Many people have long hoped they could ditch physical forms of identification, such as driver's licenses and passports, and simply present digital ID from their iPhone or Apple Watch.

That future may still be some way off, but Apple got the ball rolling back in 2021, when it announced plans to allow iPhone users to add their driver's license or state ID to the Wallet app. So far, 14 states have adopted the feature:

  • Arizona
  • Arkansas
  • California
  • Colorado
  • Georgia
  • Hawaii
  • Illinois
  • Iowa
  • Maryland
  • Montana
  • New Mexico
  • North Dakota
  • Ohio
  • West Virginia

Backend assets discovered by MacRumors indicate that Oklahoma will soon be joining that list.

We previously provided a detailed walkthrough of how to add a driver's license or state ID to the Wallet app on iPhone. As noted at the time, it's important to keep in mind that the digital ID is not a complete replacement for the physical document, so for now we'd recommend continuing to carry the "plastic version" (physical card).

However, the digital version can help protect your privacy at eligible TSA checkpoints, as well as in situations where you need to prove your age to a business. The system only confirms that you meet the age requirement and does not reveal any personal information, such as your date of birth.
